answer.rationale: Write-path p99 began climbing ~30 minutes after the day-74 release and is now 5x during peak settlement writes. memory_b1 is the only close precedent for a post-release checkout failure cleared by rolling back to a known-stable build without dropping customer writes; I am verifying that archive because the precedent was an error spike, not write latency under settlement load, so transfer is uncertain. I am not acting on the other memories: b3 is pre-peak headroom, not a demonstrated mid-peak fix and may not help a release regression; b5 offloads report reads, which does not address a write-heavy path; b2 has no regional failure signal; b4 fail-fast would shed customer writes and violates the objective. Settlement writes are downstream value at risk, so the rollback stays a small guarded cohort rather than a full cutover while cause (release vs peak vs both) remains unidentified.
